findings.title: Changing the arrival date on the berth list is only reachable through an unlabelled three-dot menu
findings.description: On the berth list the stay summary (date, time, nights) is plain text with no control next to it. The only way to change the date is the 'Change dates' link inside the 'More options' menu, shown as a three-dot icon button with no visible text.
findings.impact: Skippers who notice they picked the wrong day, or who change their mind after seeing prices, cannot see how to change the date, so they restart from the first page or phone the office.

factor_notes.frequency: Reported in tickets, survey, reviews and the usability sessions; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: In sessions people searched 38-75 s; some never found it and restarted or said they would phone.
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs every time someone needs to change dates.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. The berth list shows the stay summary as a plain paragraph with no control. #more-button is an icon-only '...' button (accessible name 'More options', no visible text). Clicking it reveals the 'Change dates' link (#change-dates), which is the only date-change control on the page.

status_history.note: Reproduced. The berth list shows the stay summary as a plain paragraph with no control. #more-button is an icon-only '...' button (accessible name 'More options', no visible text). Clicking it reveals the 'Change dates' link (#change-dates), which is the only date-change control on the page.

ratings.note: f1: only skippers who need to change the date, though the most-reported issue (15/100); i3: session participants searched 38-75 s, some restarted or said they would phone (support contact); p1: once found under the three dots it is known, but use is a few times a season. s=4; rated 3 because restarting from the short first page is a working, if costly, recovery.

Crop confirms date summary is plain text and only an unlabelled three-dot button; strongest signal (15/100, 16 sources), sessions searched 38-75 s, some restarted or would phone (support contact). Met only by those changing dates; learnable. s=4; I rate 3 because restarting from page one loses only the date/time entry, not data or money.

Frequency: 15/100 feedback items, the most reported, and date changes are a core task. Impact: 38-75 s searches, restarts and some phone calls (step-02 shows only an unlabelled '...' button). Persistence: overcome once found, though infrequent use means it is easily forgotten. s=3.

findings.title: 'Booking stopped' page gives only a code, no reason and no way back
findings.description: On the boat page, when the entered length exceeds the chosen berth's maximum (e.g. 10.4 on B14, max 10 m), the form is replaced by 'Booking stopped. This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' It does not say the boat is too long for the berth, does not offer a larger berth, and has no link or button back to the berth list or the form.

criteria.name: Help users recognise, diagnose and recover from errors

findings.impact: Skippers whose boat does not fit cannot tell what went wrong or how to continue; they abandon, restart and retype, or phone the office.

factor_notes.frequency: Hit by anyone whose length is above the berth limit; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: Observed abandonment and a moderator intervention in sessions.
factor_notes.persistence: Every time the length exceeds the berth limit.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced on B14 with length 10.4. Also reproduced on Wall berth 2 with length 34. The main content is replaced by the heading 'Booking stopped' and the text 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' Main has no reason, no alternative berth and no back or edit control.

status_history.note: Reproduced on B14 with length 10.4. Also reproduced on Wall berth 2 with length 34. The main content is replaced by the heading 'Booking stopped' and the text 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' Main has no reason, no alternative berth and no back or edit control.

ratings.note: f1: only when length exceeds the chosen berth (11/100, fed by the LOA and unit ambiguities); i3: screenshot shows a dead end with only a code, observed abandonment, retyping and phone calls; p2: the page never says why, so users cannot learn to avoid it. s=4.

Crop shows 'Booking stopped... Reference BK-409' with no reason and no way back; hit by anyone whose length exceeds the berth (11/100, 12 sources); observed abandonment, retyping, phone calls and moderator help; recurs every time. s=4.

Frequency: 11/100, only when the length exceeds the berth limit. Impact: final.png shows a dead end with only a code, no reason and no way back, so users abandon, retype or phone. Persistence: once the cause is known, users can restart with a larger berth. s=4.

findings.title: Boat details are cleared when returning to the boat page with Back
findings.description: The boat form is reset whenever the page is shown, including when the browser's Back button returns to it (e.g. from the review page), so boat name, length, draught and MMSI must all be retyped.
findings.impact: Skippers typing on a phone at sea or at anchor must re-enter all boat details to correct one value; some decline and abandon.

factor_notes.frequency: Anyone who goes back to correct a boat detail; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: All four fields lost; observed refusal to retype in a session.

verification_check.reason: Could not perform a real browser Back. Probe has no back action. Alt+ArrowLeft left the page on review.html (probe 4, step 10 failed). goto javascript:history.back() is refused by the probe's URL guard (probe 5). A fresh goto to boat.html shows an empty form, but that is a new navigation and does not test Back or bfcache restoration. Needs a manual check: fill the boat form, continue to review, press browser Back, and see whether the fields are empty.

findings.needs_human: Could not perform a real browser Back. Probe has no back action. Alt+ArrowLeft left the page on review.html (probe 4, step 10 failed). goto javascript:history.back() is refused by the probe's URL guard (probe 5). A fresh goto to boat.html shows an empty form, but that is a new navigation and does not test Back or bfcache restoration. Needs a manual check: fill the boat form, continue to review, press browser Back, and see whether the fields are empty.

findings.title: Length field does not say whether it means hull length or length overall (LOA)
findings.description: The boat page field is labelled only 'Length', with no hint. Nothing says the berth limit applies to overall length including bowsprit or davits, so people enter hull length.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

findings.impact: Skippers can enter a hull length that fits the berth when the boat overall does not, and book a berth their boat will not fit.

factor_notes.frequency: Any boat with a bowsprit, davits or similar overhang; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: Wrong berth booked; observed wrong entry in a session.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. label[for=loa] reads only 'Length' with no hint text. The draught field does have a hint. Neither the boat page nor the berth list ('Boats up to 10 metres') says whether the limit is LOA including bowsprit or davits.

status_history.note: Reproduced. label[for=loa] reads only 'Length' with no hint text. The draught field does have a hint. Neither the boat page nor the berth list ('Boats up to 10 metres') says whether the limit is LOA including bowsprit or davits.

ratings.note: f1: boats with a bowsprit, davits or other overhang (6/100); i3: screenshot confirms bare 'Length' label, wrong berth booked and office contact reported; p0: once a skipper learns the limit is LOA they enter it next time. s=3.

Crop shows bare 'Length' with no LOA hint; boats with bowsprits or davits (6/100, wrong entry observed in a session) book a berth they do not fit, discovered on arrival; ambiguity recurs each booking. s=3.

Frequency: 6/100, boats with an overhang. Impact: a wrong berth is booked and a support contact follows (FB-0004, FB-0025); step-01 shows a bare 'Length' label. Persistence: users who learn it is LOA enter it correctly next time. s=4; rated 3 because payment is on arrival and the office can reassign the berth, so no money is lost and the error is recoverable.

findings.title: Length field states no unit and accepts any positive number
findings.description: The 'Length' field shows no unit (the draught field says 'in metres') and accepts any positive number, so a length typed in feet (e.g. 34) is taken as metres with no unit prompt or plausibility check.
findings.impact: Skippers used to feet can enter the wrong unit and either be stopped without explanation or be given a berth that does not fit.

factor_notes.frequency: Skippers who think in feet; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: Wrong berth or an unexplained stop.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. The label 'Length' gives no unit, while 'Draught in metres' does. A length of 0.3 on C3 was accepted and went to review (probe 8). A length of 34 (a feet value) on Wall berth 2 was taken as metres and led to the unexplained 'Booking stopped' page (probe 9). There was no unit prompt or plausibility message.

status_history.note: Reproduced. The label 'Length' gives no unit, while 'Draught in metres' does. A length of 0.3 on C3 was accepted and went to review (probe 8). A length of 34 (a feet value) on Wall berth 2 was taken as metres and led to the unexplained 'Booking stopped' page (probe 9). There was no unit prompt or plausibility message.

ratings.note: f1: skippers who think in feet (4/100); i3: probe 8 shows any positive length accepted, a 34 ft boat got an 8 m berth and the office had to correct it; p0: learned after one correction. s=3.
Crop shows 'Length' with no unit while draught says metres; skippers thinking in feet (4/100) can get a wrong berth (one caught by the office) or an unexplained stop; learnable once noticed. s=3.

Frequency: 4/100, skippers who think in feet. Impact: a berth too small is booked or the user hits the unexplained stop; the office caught it in FB-0091. Persistence: avoided once noticed. s=4; rated 3 because of the lowest observed count and the office catching it before arrival, with no money lost.

findings.title: MMSI is required with no explanation and no option for boats without one
findings.description: The boat page has a field labelled only 'MMSI', with no hint; submitting it empty shows 'Enter the MMSI'. Nothing explains what an MMSI is, where to find it, or what to do if the boat has no DSC radio.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

findings.impact: Skippers of small or chartered boats without a DSC radio, or who do not know the term, cannot complete the boat page and must phone.

factor_notes.frequency: See linked feedback; several session participants stopped here.
factor_notes.impact: Blocks the booking for boats without an MMSI; a moderator hint was needed in one session.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. label[for=mmsi] reads 'MMSI' with no hint. Submitting the form empty gives 'Enter the MMSI' (#mmsi-error and the summary link). No text explains the term or offers an option for boats without an MMSI.

status_history.note: Reproduced. label[for=mmsi] reads 'MMSI' with no hint. Submitting the form empty gives 'Enter the MMSI' (#mmsi-error and the summary link). No text explains the term or offers an option for boats without an MMSI.

ratings.note: f2: 10/100 reports and several session participants stopped; small and chartered boats are a common visitor type; i3: required field with no hint blocks the booking for boats without DSC, users phoned; p2: a boat without an MMSI can never get past it. s=4.

Crop shows bare 'MMSI' label, required with no hint or opt-out; boats without DSC (10/100, session stops, moderator hint) cannot complete the critical booking journey and must phone; recurs every booking for them. s=4.

Frequency: 10/100, boats without DSC and people who do not know the term. Impact: the booking cannot be completed online and users phone (the field is a bare 'MMSI' label in step-01). Persistence: boats without an MMSI can never get past it. s=4.

findings.title: Tide table is in UTC while arrival times are local, with no conversion
findings.description: The tide table on the first page gives high water in UTC (stated only in the table caption) while the arrival-time list above it is in local time. In summer time skippers must add an hour themselves, and people read the table as local time.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

findings.impact: Skippers who read the times as local plan the gate an hour wrong and arrive to a closed gate or wait outside.

factor_notes.frequency: Anyone arriving during summer time; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: Physical consequence: waiting outside the gate.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. The table.tides caption reads 'High water at the quay, times in UTC'. The cells give UTC times, for example Sat 17 Oct 02:08 and 14:32. The arrival-time select offers plain clock times with no zone, and no converted local time appears anywhere. 17 Oct 2026 falls in UK summer time, so the table is an hour off from local clock time.

status_history.note: Reproduced. The table.tides caption reads 'High water at the quay, times in UTC'. The cells give UTC times, for example Sat 17 Oct 02:08 and 14:32. The arrival-time select offers plain clock times with no zone, and no converted local time appears anywhere. 17 Oct 2026 falls in UK summer time, so the table is an hour off from local clock time.

ratings.note: f2: every summer-time arrival (8/100 reports); i2: screenshot shows UTC only in the caption next to local arrival times, users arrived an hour off and waited at a closed gate; p1: learned once noticed. s=3.

Crop shows table caption 'times in UTC' above local arrival times; anyone arriving in summer time (8/100, session participant read 14:32 as local); consequence is planning the gate an hour wrong and waiting outside; once learned it is overcome. s=3.

Frequency: 8/100, and it affects every summer-time arrival (step-01 shows only the caption 'times in UTC'). Impact: gate timing an hour wrong, so users wait outside or arrive to a closed gate. Persistence: overcome once the user notices UTC. s=3.

findings.title: Arrival time can be set when the sill gate is closed, with no warning
findings.description: The arrival-time select offers 06:00-21:00 on every date regardless of the tide. Choosing a time outside the gate window (about two hours either side of high water) is accepted with no warning on the first page or later.
findings.impact: Skippers book an arrival they cannot make and find a shut gate.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. On 17 Oct, high water is 02:08 and 14:32 UTC and the gate is open about ±2 h, so 09:00 is outside every gate window in both UTC and local time. I chose 09:00 and completed the whole flow: berths, boat, review, then 'Booking confirmed'. There was no warning at any step. The select offers 06:00-21:00 whatever the tide.

status_history.note: Reproduced. On 17 Oct, high water is 02:08 and 14:32 UTC and the gate is open about ±2 h, so 09:00 is outside every gate window in both UTC and local time. I chose 09:00 and completed the whole flow: berths, boat, review, then 'Booking confirmed'. There was no warning at any step. The select offers 06:00-21:00 whatever the tide.

ratings.note: f2: most listed times fall outside the gate window on any day (7/100 reports); i2: the booking accepts an arrival the boat cannot make, found out at the shut gate; p1: skippers who learn the gate plan around it themselves. s=3.

Time select offers 06:00-21:00 regardless of tide; affects those choosing outside the gate window (7/100); consequence is arriving at a shut gate and waiting, a significant error though skippers can usually adjust at sea; no warning on any booking. s=3.

Frequency: 7/100, arrivals chosen without cross-checking the tide. Impact: a booking for an arrival time the boat cannot make, with no warning at any step. Persistence: tide-aware skippers learn to check the table themselves. s=3.

findings.title: Berth list shows only a per-metre-per-night rate, not the total for the stay
findings.description: Each berth option shows a price such as '£3.20 per metre per night'; the total appears only on the review page, after boat details are entered. Comparing berths means multiplying rate, length and nights by hand.
findings.impact: Skippers comparing berths on a phone must calculate totals themselves before choosing.

factor_notes.impact: Extra effort; a session participant used a phone calculator for about 45 s.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. Each .berth-price reads '£x.xx per metre per night'. The berth list shows no total. The total (£74.88 for C3, 10.4 m, 2 nights) first appears on the review page, after the boat details are entered.

status_history.note: Reproduced. Each .berth-price reads '£x.xx per metre per night'. The berth list shows no total. The total (£74.88 for C3, 10.4 m, 2 nights) first appears on the review page, after the boat details are entered.

ratings.note: f3: every berth comparison (screenshot shows only per-metre rates); i1: extra effort, a participant used a calculator for about 45 s; p2: recurs every booking. s=3; rated 2 because the total does appear on review before committing, so no wrong payment results, only effort.

Crop shows only per-metre-per-night rates; every comparing skipper must multiply by hand (7/100 reports, ~45 s calculator use in session) and it recurs each booking. s=3; I rate 2 because the cost is effort only, with no wrong choice or abandonment observed and the total appears before confirming.

Frequency: 7/100, though every comparison involves it. Impact: mental arithmetic, about 45 s with a calculator, no errors (step-02 shows rates only). Persistence: every booking. s=3; rated 2 because per-metre-per-night is the standard marina pricing convention these users know, and the cost is delay only.

findings.title: The thing being booked is called a berth, a pontoon space and a mooring on different pages
findings.description: The first page says 'Book a visitor berth', the berth list says 'Choose a pontoon space', the review page says 'Check your mooring booking', and the summary row says 'Berth'.
findings.impact: First-time visitors are unsure whether they booked the right thing or whether the terms mean different prices.

factor_notes.impact: Hesitation and re-checking; no observed failure.

verification_check.reason: Reproduced. The h1 headings read 'Book a visitor berth' (/), 'Choose a pontoon space' (/berths.html) and 'Check your mooring booking' (/review.html). The review summary row is labelled 'Berth'. The berth options mix 'Pontoon A, berth 6' and 'Wall berth 2'.

status_history.note: Reproduced. The h1 headings read 'Book a visitor berth' (/), 'Choose a pontoon space' (/berths.html) and 'Check your mooring booking' (/review.html). The review summary row is labelled 'Berth'. The berth options mix 'Pontoon A, berth 6' and 'Wall berth 2'.

ratings.note: f2: every first-time visitor sees berth/pontoon space/mooring across pages (5/100); i1: hesitation and doubt about price, no failure observed; p0: mostly a first-visit confusion. s=2.

Every booker sees the shifting terms (berth/pontoon space/mooring, confirmed in probes and crop) but only 5/100 reported confusion; impact is hesitation and price doubt, no failure; mostly a first-visit hurdle. s=2.

Frequency: 5/100, but every user sees berth, pontoon space and mooring (step-02 heading 'Choose a pontoon space'). Impact: hesitation and doubt about price, no failure observed. Persistence: mainly first visits. s=2.

findings.title: No indication of the current step or how many steps remain
findings.description: None of the booking pages (plan, berth list, boat, review) shows a step indicator or 'step x of y'.
findings.impact: Skippers on patchy mobile signal cannot judge whether to finish now or wait for coverage.

verification_check.reason: I confirmed the absence myself. I searched all five pages (/, berths, boat, review, confirmed) in their ARIA snapshots and screenshots. None has a step indicator, progress list or 'step x of y' text.

status_history.note: I confirmed the absence myself. I searched all five pages (/, berths, boat, review, confirmed) in their ARIA snapshots and screenshots. None has a step indicator, progress list or 'step x of y' text.

ratings.note: f3: every booking page lacks a step indicator (7/100); i1: uncertainty, no observed failure or abandonment; p1: returning users know the flow length. s=3; rated 2 because the flow is short and no behavioural harm was observed, only self-reported unease.

No step indicator on any page (probes), met by everyone; impact is uncertainty with no observed failure; partly learned by returning users. s=3; I rate 2 because the flow is short and nothing in the evidence shows abandonment caused by it.
Frequency: 7/100 reports, but every user is affected on every page. Impact: uncertainty on patchy signal, no failure observed. Persistence: returning skippers know the short flow. s=2.

findings.title: Confirmation page gives no arrival instructions (VHF channel, gate times)
findings.description: The confirmation page shows the reference, arrival date, berth and nights and a link to book again. It does not give the VHF channel to call, the gate opening times on the arrival day, or what to do on arrival.
findings.impact: Arriving skippers must phone the office or wait outside the harbour to find out how to enter.

factor_notes.frequency: Every completed booking; see linked feedback.
factor_notes.impact: Phone calls; one report of a 40-minute wait outside.

verification_check.reason: I confirmed the absence myself after completing a booking. The confirmed.html main area contains only the reference SQ-1017-C3, the arrival date (no time), the berth, the nights and 'Book another visit'. There is no VHF channel, no gate times for the arrival day and no arrival instructions. The footer gives only the office phone number and hours.

status_history.note: I confirmed the absence myself after completing a booking. The confirmed.html main area contains only the reference SQ-1017-C3, the arrival date (no time), the berth, the nights and 'Book another visit'. There is no VHF channel, no gate times for the arrival day and no arrival instructions. The footer gives only the office phone number and hours.

ratings.note: f2: every first-time visitor (screenshot shows reference, date, berth, nights only); i3: phone calls and one 40-minute wait outside reported; p0: returning skippers already know the channel and gate. s=4; rated 3 because the office number is on the page and VHF channels and gate times are also in pilot books skippers normally carry.

Every confirmation lacks VHF channel and gate times, mattering mostly to first-time visitors (7/100); consequence is phone calls and one 40-minute wait outside, after the booking task itself succeeded; returning skippers know the routine. s=3.

Frequency: 7/100, and every completed booking is affected. Impact: phone calls (a support contact) and one 40-minute wait outside. Persistence: returning visitors know the channel. s=4; rated 3 because the booking itself succeeds, the office number is on every page, and the information is a standard pilot-book item.

findings.title: Booking pages reported as slow or timing out on weak mobile signal
findings.description: Reporters say the booking pages were slow, timed out on 4G, or did not load at anchor. To check: page weight and load time under throttled mobile network conditions.
findings.impact: Skippers booking from the water may be unable to load or complete the flow.

factor_notes.impact: One reporter attributes it to having no signal at all.

verification_check.reason: I could not reproduce weak-signal conditions because probe has no network throttling or offline emulation. Unthrottled against localhost, / loaded in 27 ms (DCL 26, FCP 28). The whole flow ran with 0 failed or 4xx/5xx requests and 0 blocked remote requests. No slowness appeared under these conditions. Needs a throttled check (for example Slow 4G in DevTools or Lighthouse mobile) to measure page weight and load time. It also needs a decision on whether 'no signal at all' is in scope.
